speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the chest pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of forceful vomiting followed by choking, coughing, and chest pain in a 51-year-old male is highly concerning for a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). I need to assess the severity of the pain and check for signs of peritonitis immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Serum Amylase and Lipase
REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay

DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome
